blocks.caption: Osmoregulation in three habitats
rows: the animal is hypertonic: water enters by osmosis (especially through the gills) and salts such as Na+ and Cl- diffuse out
produces large volumes of dilute urine; actively transports salts back in; rarely drinks
bony fishes are hypotonic: water leaves through gills and skin, and salts diffuse in and come with swallowed sea water
drinks sea water; makes small amounts of concentrated urine; chloride cells in the gills pump salts out using ATP; kidneys remove salts; some have rectal salt glands
water is lost by evaporation from breathing surfaces and skin and in wastes

waterproof coverings (chitin and wax in insects, keratin scales in reptiles, keratinized skin and oil glands in birds and mammals); water-saving kidneys; urea or uric acid instead of ammonia; behaviour such as staying underground by day

blocks.text: Many desert animals stay underground in the heat of the day and come out at night when the air is cooler and more humid, feeding on carbohydrate-rich seeds. The kangaroo rat can survive entirely on metabolic water, produced as a by-product of cellular respiration.

Some invertebrates such as tardigrades (water bears) survive losing almost all their body water by entering a dormant state called anhydrobiosis, and return to active life years later when water returns.

blocks.caption: Osmoregulation, nitrogenous wastes and human thermoregulation (original diagram after topics 13.2 and 13.3).
blocks.long_description: A freshwater fish is saltier than the water around it, so water keeps entering by osmosis and salts leak out; it produces a large volume of dilute urine and takes salts back in by active transport, and rarely drinks. A marine bony fish is less salty than sea water, so it loses water and gains salt; it drinks sea water, makes little concentrated urine and uses chloride cells in its gills to pump salt out. Ammonia needs about 500 mL of water per gram to excrete safely, urea about 50 mL and uric acid about 1 mL, so animals short of water excrete urea or uric acid. When the human body is too hot, skin vessels widen and sweat cools it; when it is too cold, skin vessels narrow, muscles shiver and hairs stand up.

blocks.prompt: Why does a freshwater fish produce dilute urine while a marine bony fish produces concentrated urine?
blocks.explanation: The freshwater fish keeps gaining water by osmosis and must get rid of the excess; the marine fish keeps losing water and must save every drop, so it excretes little, concentrated urine.

items: Fresh water: gain water, lose salt, dilute urine. Sea water: lose water, gain salt, drink and pump salt out. Land: waterproof coverings and water-saving excretion.
